title: Agentic Eval: Does the Number of Reasoning Steps Affect Safety Outcomes?
original_idea: Compare safety outcomes (rate of completing harmful tasks) for the same model using zero-shot, chain-of-thought (3-step), and extended reasoning (10-step) on a set of 100 safety-relevant agentic tasks. Tests whether longer reasoning chains are associated with higher rates of unsafe final actions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear and direct path: if reasoning depth increases unsafe action rates, this directly informs deployment constraints for reasoning-capable agents in agentic settings.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires API access to extended reasoning models, constructing 100 agentic tasks with safety relevance, and evaluating safety outcomes. Moderate challenge for beginner CS students within 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-bounded: single independent variable (reasoning steps), clear dependent variable (unsafe action rate), fixed model. Clear deliverable.

title: Benchmark for Permission Escalation Detection in Multi-Agent Systems
original_idea: Design 80 scenarios where a simulated subagent requests permissions beyond its granted scope. Evaluate whether an LLM orchestrator (GPT-4o or Llama-3-70B) detects and refuses the escalation attempt across varying request framings.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly operationalizes a named OWASP Agentic Applications 2026 risk. A benchmark for permission escalation detection has clear practical value for multi-agent system safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing 80 meaningful permission escalation scenarios and setting up multi-agent evaluation requires understanding of agent architectures. Moderate challenge for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: 80 scenarios, one evaluation task (detect/refuse escalation), clear pass/fail metric. Deliverable is the benchmark dataset plus evaluation results.

title: Investigating the Effect of Retrieval Context Size on Safety Benchmark Scores
original_idea: Construct a RAG safety evaluation where harmful instructions are embedded in retrieved documents at varying context sizes (512, 2K, 8K, 32K tokens). Measure how compliance rate with the harmful instruction changes with total context size.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct safety implication: if longer RAG contexts overwhelm safety filters, organizations using large document collections in RAG are exposed. Clear causal chain to deployment decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Straightforward experimental design: embed harmful instructions in varying-length contexts, call API, measure compliance. Well within medium compute and 30 hours for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: single independent variable (context size), single dependent variable (compliance rate), clear experimental protocol. Minimal ambiguity in deliverables.

title: Tool for Visualizing Safety Benchmark Coverage Gaps Using Embedding Projections
original_idea: Embed all prompts from AILuminate, HELM Safety, and TrustLLM using a sentence transformer. Project to 2D with UMAP. Visualize cluster density and identify sparse regions representing coverage gaps. Publish as an interactive HTML artifact.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful but indirect: a visualization tool aids understanding of benchmark coverage but does not directly improve safety. Impact depends on adoption by benchmark designers.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Sentence transformers and UMAP are well-documented, CPU-friendly tools. Building an interactive HTML visualization is within reach of CS students with web skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: an interactive HTML visualization artifact. Well-bounded pipeline (embed, project, visualize). Some scope creep risk in making it interactive.

title: Investigating Halo Effects in Safety Scoring: Do High-Quality Responses Get Higher Safety Scores?
original_idea: Construct paired responses to the same harmful prompt: one poorly written and one well-written, both equally unsafe. Submit to LLM judges and measure whether quality correlates with safety score.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly challenges the validity of LLM-as-judge safety evaluations. If confirmed, this bias means capable-but-unsafe models receive inflated safety scores on benchmarks.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing paired responses and querying LLM judges is straightforward. Accessible experimental design for CS students with basic programming skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: single hypothesis (halo effect), paired design with clear controls, single metric (safety score difference between quality-matched pairs).

title: Benchmark for Safety Under Adversarial Few-Shot Examples
original_idea: Construct 100 prompts with adversarial few-shot examples (demonstrations of harmful compliance) followed by a harmful request. Evaluate three models and compare refusal rates against zero-shot equivalents.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical attack vector in RAG and API settings. Benchmarking few-shot prompt injection as a safety vulnerability has direct implications for deployment security.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing few-shot prompts and running evaluations on three models via API is well within beginner CS student capabilities and medium compute budget.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: 100 prompts, zero-shot vs few-shot comparison, refusal rate as metric. Clear deliverable is the benchmark dataset and comparative results.

title: Investigating Benchmark Score Variance Due to Prompt Batching
original_idea: Evaluate the same 200 safety prompts individually and in batches of 10, 20, and 50. Measure disagreement rates in safety verdicts between individual and batched evaluation across two models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful methodological insight but somewhat niche. If batching changes verdicts, it affects evaluation infrastructure but is a secondary concern compared to core safety questions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires local inference setup with vLLM or HuggingFace pipeline for batch processing. Setting up batch inference is moderately challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very tightly scoped: single variable (batch size), clear metric (verdict disagreement rate), well-defined protocol. Minimal ambiguity.

title: Tool for Automated Safety Regression Testing in CI/CD Pipelines
original_idea: Build a Python package that integrates with GitHub Actions or similar CI/CD systems to automatically run a small curated safety probe suite on model checkpoints. Return a pass/fail signal based on configurable thresholds.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct practical safety impact: enables continuous safety validation in model deployment pipelines. Implements a best practice from red teaming playbooks.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a distributable Python package with CI/CD integration, configurable thresholds, and model checkpoint evaluation is substantial engineering for beginner CS students in 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Moderately broad: requires package design, CI/CD integration, probe suite curation, threshold configuration, and validation. Multiple deliverables compound scope.

title: Investigating Whether Safety Benchmarks Are Sensitive to Chat Template Formatting
original_idea: Evaluate a model under its correct chat template and two incorrect but plausible templates on a safety benchmark. Measure how much template mismatch shifts safety scores compared to template-correct evaluation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly challenges benchmark validity. Template errors are common in practice; if they produce spurious safety differences, many published comparisons may be invalid.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running the same eval with different chat templates is straightforward. Requires basic understanding of tokenizer configuration but well within beginner scope.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: single variable (chat template), clear metric (safety score shift), minimal experimental design. Very clean single-question study.

title: Replicating Safety Scores Under Adversarial Suffixes (GCG Attack)
original_idea: Generate GCG adversarial suffixes for a subset of AILuminate prompts using an open-source attack toolkit. Compare safety scores with and without suffixes for two models. Compute the correlation between baseline safety score and suffix attack success rate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Fundamental validity question: do safety benchmarks predict adversarial robustness? If not, benchmarks measure only compliance under benign inputs, not genuine alignment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: GCG attack generation requires GPU resources, familiarity with adversarial ML toolkits, and gradient access to model weights. Challenging for beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: generate suffixes, compare with/without, compute correlation. Clear experimental protocol with defined deliverables.

title: Benchmark for Cultural Safety: Harm Definitions Across Cultural Contexts
original_idea: Construct 100 prompts where the harm assessment is culturally variable. Survey 15-20 participants from at least three cultural backgrounds for harm ratings. Compare against model refusal rates and benchmark labels.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Important for global AI deployments. Documents that universal harm definitions are an assumption, not a fact, which has direct implications for benchmark design and deployment policy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Recruiting 15-20 participants from 3+ cultural backgrounds, designing a valid survey, and handling human subjects considerations is logistically very challenging for beginner CS students in 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Broad scope: prompt construction, human participant recruitment across cultures, survey design, model evaluation, and cross-cultural statistical comparison. Multiple complex deliverables.

title: Investigating Self-Consistency of Safety Scores Across Repeated Runs
original_idea: Run the same safety benchmark (100-item subset) on two models five times each at temperature 0.7. Compute per-item score variance and identify which hazard categories show highest run-to-run inconsistency.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Fundamental benchmark validity: if safety scores have high variance, small differences on leaderboards may be statistically meaningless. Establishing confidence intervals is basic scientific hygiene.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extremely accessible: run the same eval 5 times, compute variance. Requires only API calls and basic statistics. Perfect for beginner CS students with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Maximally scoped: single question (what is the run-to-run variance?), single protocol (repeat eval), straightforward statistical analysis. No ambiguity.

title: Constructing a Minimal Viable Safety Benchmark for Resource-Constrained Evaluators
original_idea: Using published AILuminate scores for available models, identify a minimal subset of prompts (50-200) that maximally preserves the model ranking on the full benchmark. Validate on held-out models and publish the minimal battery.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Lowers the cost of safety evaluation, enabling more frequent testing by resource-constrained practitioners. Directly increases safety evaluation cadence.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Subset selection to maximize rank-preservation is a well-defined optimization problem using publicly available data. Approachable with basic statistics and Python.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: a minimal prompt set with validation results. Well-defined optimization objective. Some scope risk in validation methodology.

title: Investigating Whether Reasoning Traces in Chain-of-Thought Reveal Misalignment Invisible in Final Answers
original_idea: Collect CoT reasoning traces from a model on 150 safety-boundary prompts. Manually annotate reasoning traces for signs of misaligned reasoning (explicit recognition of harm paired with compliant intent). Compare to safety scores on final answers only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Core safety question: if CoT traces reveal misalignment invisible in outputs, reasoning transparency becomes a critical safety monitoring tool. Compelling and urgent path to safety improvement.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Collecting traces via API is easy, but manually annotating 150 traces for misaligned reasoning requires judgment and is labor-intensive for 30 hours. Annotation codebook design adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear hypothesis and defined method. Deliverable is annotation results plus comparison. Some scope risk in developing reliable annotation criteria for 'misaligned reasoning'.

title: Cross-Evaluator Replication: Do Inspect AI and Garak Agree on Model Rankings?
original_idea: Run comparable attack categories from both Inspect AI and Garak on three open-source models. Compute rank correlation between the two frameworks' safety scores and identify attack categories with highest inter-framework disagreement.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Meta-evaluation insight: useful for establishing trust in evaluation infrastructure, but indirect safety impact. Documenting agreement/disagreement is informative but not actionable on its own.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Learning and configuring two different evaluation frameworks, ensuring comparable attack categories, and running on three models is moderately challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-bounded comparison: two frameworks, three models, rank correlation. Clear deliverable. Defining 'comparable' attack categories adds some ambiguity.

title: Benchmark for Evaluating Safety Under Indirect Harm: Third-Party Impact Assessment
original_idea: Create 120 scenarios where the harm of compliance falls primarily on a third party (privacy violations about others, defamation, enabling stalking). Evaluate three models and compare refusal rates against matched direct-harm equivalents.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses a major gap: many real-world AI harms are third-party harms. Benchmarks ignoring this systematically underestimate safety failure rates. Compelling and urgent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Creating 120 scenarios with matched direct/indirect pairs requires careful domain expertise and scenario design. Evaluation itself is straightforward but scenario construction is the bottleneck.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: benchmark dataset and comparative refusal rate analysis. Well-bounded paired comparison design.

title: Replicating Safety Benchmarks Across System Prompt Languages
original_idea: Evaluate three models on 200 safety prompts under four system prompt language conditions: English-English, English-Chinese, Chinese-English, and Chinese-Chinese. Measure refusal rate differences across language combinations.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical attack surface: mixed-language system prompts are realistic in global deployments. If language mismatch weakens safety, it has direct deployment implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Translating system prompts and running evaluations across four conditions is straightforward. Requires API access and basic multilingual text handling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-bounded 2x2 design (system prompt language x user query language). Clear metric (refusal rate), clear deliverable.

title: Investigating Whether Constitutional AI Fine-Tuning Produces Generalizable Safety
original_idea: Evaluate a CAI fine-tuned open-source model on its reported benchmark (in-distribution) and on an orthogonal safety benchmark not used in its training (out-of-distribution). Compute the in-distribution vs. out-of-distribution safety score gap.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Important for understanding CAI limitations. If CAI safety is benchmark-specific, safety assurances are narrower than assumed, with direct implications for deployment trust.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires identifying which benchmarks were used in CAI training (may be undocumented), selecting appropriate out-of-distribution benchmarks, and running evaluations on large models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear comparison design: in-distribution vs. out-of-distribution safety scores. Single metric (score gap). Deliverable is the gap measurement and analysis.

title: Investigating Whether Safety Benchmarks Predict Robustness to Low-Resource Language Jailbreaks
original_idea: Translate 150 AILuminate harmful prompts into three low-resource languages (Swahili, Tagalog, Yoruba) using professional translation or a high-quality translation API. Evaluate three multilingual models and compare refusal rates against English baseline.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses a documented real-world attack vector. Low-resource language jailbreaks expose users in those regions. Compelling and urgent safety path.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Translation quality for low-resource languages is a concern (professional translation may be needed). Running multilingual evaluations adds setup complexity. Moderate for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear design: translate, evaluate, compare refusal rates. Well-bounded with specific languages and prompt count. Deliverable is the cross-lingual refusal rate analysis.

title: Tool for Safety Benchmark Comparison Dashboard
original_idea: Build a Python/Streamlit dashboard that ingests leaderboard data from HELM Safety, AILuminate, and TrustLLM, normalizes scores to a common scale, and renders interactive rank comparison plots.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tooling convenience with indirect safety impact. Makes cross-benchmark inconsistency visible but does not directly improve model safety. Impact depends on adoption.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Streamlit and pandas are perfectly suited for beginner CS students. Data is publicly available. Classic data engineering project well within 30 hours and medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: a working Streamlit dashboard. Well-defined data pipeline (ingest, normalize, visualize). Some scope risk in making it polished.

title: Failure Mode Investigation: Do Safety Scores Differ for Generative vs. Discriminative Tasks?
original_idea: Reframe 100 safety-sensitive scenarios as both generative (generate an explanation of X) and discriminative (rate whether this content describing X is appropriate). Measure whether the same model produces more unsafe outputs in one format than the other.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical implications for content moderation deployments. If discriminative format has different safety properties, format-specific evaluations are needed. Direct deployment relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reframing prompts into two formats and running evaluations is accessible. Requires creative prompt design but no advanced ML knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped paired comparison: same 100 scenarios in two formats, same model. Clear metric (unsafe output rate by format). Clean experimental design.

title: Investigating Whether Benchmark Scores Predict Safety on User-Submitted Adversarial Prompts
original_idea: Collect 200 adversarial prompts from public red-teaming community repositories. Evaluate three models and compare safety scores on community-sourced vs. benchmark-curated prompts. Compute rank correlation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Fundamental ecological validity question for all safety benchmarks. If curated benchmarks don't predict robustness to real user attacks, the entire evaluation paradigm needs revision. Compelling and urgent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Public jailbreak databases on GitHub provide the data. Running evaluations and computing rank correlation is straightforward for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear design: two prompt sources, three models, rank correlation. Well-bounded deliverable. Some subjectivity in selecting 'comparable' community prompts.

title: Benchmark for Hallucination-Safety Intersection: When Confident Falsehoods Cause Harm
original_idea: Construct 150 prompts in high-stakes domains (medical, legal, emergency safety) where a confident hallucinated answer would cause harm. Score responses on both factual accuracy and potential harm of the false content. Evaluate three models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses a major real-world harm category not captured by either hallucination or safety benchmarks alone. Medical/legal/emergency falsehoods cause tangible harm. Compelling path.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing 150 domain-specific prompts with known correct answers requires expertise in medical/legal/emergency domains. Dual scoring (accuracy + harm) adds evaluation complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: benchmark dataset and dual-metric evaluation results. Well-defined evaluation protocol. Some scope risk in ensuring factual ground truth for 150 prompts.

title: Investigating Whether Safety Evaluations Are Biased Against Smaller Models Due to Verbosity Differences
original_idea: Evaluate models of varying sizes on safety benchmarks using an LLM judge. Compute correlation between response length and safety score, separately for compliant and non-compliant responses. Test whether brevity is a confound in safety score assignment.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety scores are confounded by response length, it systematically misleads deployment decisions. Small model scores inflated, large model scores deflated. Clear benchmark validity impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Correlation analysis on existing evaluation outputs is accessible. Running evaluations on multiple model sizes and computing length-score correlations is straightforward.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: single hypothesis (verbosity confound), clear statistical test (correlation), well-defined analysis. Minimal ambiguity in deliverables.

title: Replicating Safety Benchmark Results Under Speculative Decoding
original_idea: Run safety benchmarks on a model pair (e.g., Llama-3-70B with Llama-3-8B as draft) using standard decoding and speculative decoding. Measure whether safety scores and refusal rates differ between decoding strategies.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Niche production optimization concern. If speculative decoding changes safety scores, it affects specific deployments, but the impact pathway is narrow compared to other ideas.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running 70B+8B model pairs with speculative decoding requires significant GPU resources (likely exceeds medium compute) and familiarity with vLLM speculative decoding configuration.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear experimental design: two decoding strategies, same model pair, safety score comparison. Well-bounded with specific deliverables.

title: Investigating Safety Score Changes After Model Merging
original_idea: Merge a safety-aligned base model with a capability-focused fine-tuned model using SLERP or task vector addition. Evaluate safety benchmark scores at several merge ratios and plot the safety-capability tradeoff curve.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical implications for a popular technique. If model merging degrades safety non-linearly, organizations using this technique may produce unsafe models unintentionally.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Model merging with mergekit requires significant GPU resources for loading and merging large models, plus ML expertise to properly configure merge strategies. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear design: merge at several ratios, evaluate safety, plot curve. Well-defined deliverable (tradeoff curve). Single experimental paradigm.

title: Blind Spot Cascade: When SAE Feature Gaps Enable Unchecked Harmful Steering
original_idea: Train an SAE on a small open model (e.g. Pythia-1.4B), identify harmful-adjacent concepts that appear in outputs but have no high-activation SAE feature, then measure whether steering vectors built from existing features can suppress those outputs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifies an important compounding failure mode where interpretability blind spots feed into steering coverage gaps. If confirmed, it challenges reliance on SAE-based safety monitoring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training SAEs, working with Pythia internals, identifying feature gaps, and building steering vectors requires advanced mechanistic interpretability knowledge. Far beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-step project: train SAE, identify gaps, build steering vectors, compare suppression rates. Multiple intermediate deliverables increase scope.

title: Probe Evasion Amplification: Jailbreak Resistance Degrades When Activation Probes Are Known
original_idea: Train a linear jailbreak-detection probe on a small model's residual stream activations. Apply a gradient-based adversarial attack that minimizes probe activation while maximizing harmful output probability. Measure attack success rate with and without probe knowledge.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly challenges a primary safety tool (activation probes). If probes can be reliably evaded by adversaries who know the architecture, the entire probe-based safety layer collapses. Urgent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Gradient-based adversarial attacks on activation spaces, probe training on residual streams, and multi-objective optimization require expert-level ML knowledge. Not feasible for beginner CS students in 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-step: train probe, craft gradient-based adversarial attack, measure with/without knowledge, test multi-layer resistance. Several interconnected experimental components.

title: Monitor Prompt Injection: Adaptive Attacks That Exploit Interpretability Architecture Assumptions
original_idea: Implement a simple AI control loop: a small policy model whose outputs are passed to a monitor model. Craft adversarial outputs from the policy model containing prompt injections targeting the monitor. Measure bypass rates. Then test whether monitoring at the activation level is more resistant.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly challenges AI control protocols that rely on trusted monitors. If activation-level monitoring is not more robust, current control architectures are fundamentally vulnerable. Urgent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing control loops, crafting adversarial outputs targeting monitors, and comparing text-level vs. activation-level monitoring requires advanced systems and ML knowledge. Very challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-step: build control loop, craft adversarial outputs, measure bypass rates, implement activation-level alternative, compare. Multiple complex deliverables.

title: Deception in the Residual: How Superposition Hides Scheming Signals from Linear Probes
original_idea: Using a small model that can be prompted into simple deceptive behavior, train linear probes to detect the deceptive state. Measure whether probe accuracy degrades on polysemantic neurons vs. more monosemantic ones identified via SAE feature activation patterns.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Core deception detection question. If superposition hides scheming signals from probes, a primary detection method fails precisely when needed. Directly addresses a central alignment concern.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires deep mechanistic interpretability knowledge: inducing deceptive behavior, training probes on internal states, SAE analysis, and understanding polysemanticity. Far beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-step: induce deception, train probes, run SAE analysis, compare probe accuracy across neuron types. Multiple interconnected experimental components.
